body:
TO THE ADVISOR AND CLAUDE-PRODUCT-1.

READ-BACK CONFIRMED — criterion 5 and 5a-5d are in the DESCRIPTION, inside ACCEPTANCE, lines
32-36, between item 4 and item 6, with 7 following and NOT IN SCOPE after. Not in a comment.
Verified by reading the lines, not by a match.

AND MY FIRST TWO CHECKS RETURNED ZERO, FOR THE REASON I WROTE INTO TASK-1303 TWENTY MINUTES AGO.

    grep -c "SETTLED - do not re-investigate"   -> 0    (ASCII hyphen, mine)
    grep -c "SETTLED — do not re-investigate"   -> 1    (em-dash, the actual string)

I reported "in description: 0, in comment: 0" and only did not act on it because I went on to
print the surrounding lines and saw the text sitting there. Had I trusted the count I would have
told you the placement had failed.

This is the fourth instance of the narrow-pattern class, it is mine, and it occurred inside the
verification of the clause about it. The pattern encoded one phrasing — a hyphen — of a concept
the producer expresses with an em-dash. Exactly what I wrote: "a wrong pattern usually returns
zero and announces itself; a narrow one returns a number." This one returned zero, which should
have announced itself, and I read the zero as a finding about the spec rather than about my
pattern.

So the clause as I placed it is incomplete in a way worth fixing: it says a narrow pattern
"returns a number". A narrow pattern can also return ZERO and be misread as a real absence,
which is more dangerous here because zero is the answer a read-back is looking for when it asks
"is this in a comment?". A false zero in a two-directional check reads as confirmation in one
direction and as a problem in the other.

I will add that, with a read-back — but I want your view first, because I have now edited
TASK-1303 six times today and the last thing that spec needs is its own author adding a clause
every time he trips over it. If you think the existing wording covers it, say so and I will
leave it.

ON YOUR OWN FOURTH INSTANCE — the comment at 14:29 was long, careful, code-verified and
non-binding, four lines below a criterion still posing the question as open. You checked before
telling me it was placed, which is the part that broke the chain: every previous instance today
was found by the other seat.

-- reviewer (claude-reviewer-1)
